# Story 1.5: Standardize Journal Fragment with Three Entry Types

## Status
Done

## Story
**As a** user,
**I want** consistent styling across Activity (auto-generated), Note, and Diary entry types in the journal,
**so that** I have a unified experience when viewing and creating different types of journal entries.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Apply consistent card styling to all three journal entry types (Activity, Note, Diary)
2. Standardize form styling for Note and Diary entry creation/editing
3. Implement consistent date picker and time selection UI across entry types
4. Apply unified typography and color scheme to entry content display
5. Ensure Activity auto-generation system maintains functionality with new styling

## Dev Notes

### Architecture Context
This story implements consistent styling for the journal fragment's three entry types (Activity, Note, Diary) as part of the UI consistency enhancement. The implementation must preserve all existing journal functionality while applying design system styling.

**Source Tree Integration:** [Source: architecture/source-tree.md#new-file-organization]
- Journal components will be placed in `features/journal/components/` package
- Journal styling resources will extend existing `values/styles.xml` structure
- Journal entry layouts will be updated to use HealthCardComponent and design system tokens

**Technology Stack:** [Source: architecture/tech-stack.md]
- **Platform:** Android API 30-36 - maintain existing API level support
- **Language:** Kotlin - continue with existing Kotlin patterns for UI components
- **UI Framework:** Material 3 - extend existing Material 3 foundation for journal components
- **Architecture:** MVVM + Navigation Components 2.9.0 - preserve existing journal architecture patterns
- **Database:** Room + Firebase - no changes to journal data persistence or sync

**Component Architecture:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#component-architecture]
- **Journal Entry Cards:** Use HealthCardComponent variants for consistent journal entry display
- **Journal Forms:** Apply HealthFormComponent styling for Note and Diary entry creation/editing
- **Integration Points:** Replaces existing journal card styling while preserving functionality
- **Key Interfaces:** Journal entry display components with Primary/Secondary card variants
- **Dependencies:** Uses HealthDesignSystem color, typography, and spacing tokens from Story 1.1

**Integration Requirements:**
- Must preserve existing journal entry data models and persistence logic
- Must maintain existing journal entry creation, editing, and deletion functionality
- Must support Activity auto-generation system without changes to generation logic
- Must maintain journal entry sync with Firebase and local Room database

**Performance Constraints:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#code-quality-standards]
- Journal styling must not increase memory usage >15% or affect startup time >200ms
- Journal entry rendering must maintain smooth scrolling performance in lists
- Must maintain existing journal performance characteristics

**File Naming Conventions:** [Source: architecture/source-tree.md#integration-guidelines]
- Continue existing camelCase for Kotlin files, snake_case for XML resources
- Journal components should use Health prefix for design system consistency
- Resource organization should extend existing values/ structure

### Component Specifications
**Journal Entry Card Components:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#unified-health-card-component]
- **Activity Entry Cards:** Use HealthCardComponent.Primary for auto-generated activity entries
- **Note Entry Cards:** Use HealthCardComponent.Secondary for user-created note entries
- **Diary Entry Cards:** Use HealthCardComponent.Secondary for user-created diary entries
- **Corner Radius:** Standardized 12dp corner radius for all journal entry cards
- **Content Padding:** HealthSpacing.Padding.standard (16dp) for journal card content

**Journal Form Components:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#consistent-form-input-system]
- **Note Creation Forms:** Apply HealthTextInputLayout styling for consistent input fields
- **Diary Creation Forms:** Apply HealthTextInputLayout styling for consistent input fields
- **Form Validation:** Use HealthFormValidation patterns for consistent error message styling and validation feedback
- **Form Buttons:** Apply HealthButton.Primary for save actions, HealthButton.Secondary for cancel actions
- **Date/Time Pickers:** Apply HealthButton.Secondary styling to date/time selection buttons with HealthTypography.Label.medium for labels

**Typography Hierarchy:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#standardized-design-system-components]
- **Entry Titles:** HealthTypography.Title.medium for journal entry headings
- **Entry Content:** HealthTypography.Body.large for main journal entry content
- **Entry Metadata:** HealthTypography.Body.small for timestamps, entry type indicators
- **Form Labels:** HealthTypography.Label.medium for form field labels

**Accessibility Requirements:** [Source: architecture/coding-standards.md#code-quality-standards]
- Minimum touch target size of 48dp for all journal entry interactions
- Proper content descriptions for screen reader support
- Focus states with HealthColors.Primary.default outline
- Keyboard navigation support for journal entry selection and editing

### Journal Feature Analysis
**Three Entry Types to Standardize:**
- **Activity Entries:** Auto-generated entries that track user health activities and metrics
- **Note Entries:** User-created text entries for quick thoughts and observations
- **Diary Entries:** User-created detailed entries for comprehensive journaling

**Journal Functionality to Preserve:**
- Activity auto-generation system and scheduling
- Note and Diary entry creation, editing, and deletion
- Journal entry search and filtering capabilities
- Journal data sync with Firebase and local Room storage
- Journal entry privacy and security features
